summary.short: FDA classification rule placing software algorithm devices that assist pathology diagnosis from scanned whole slide images in Class II, subject to special controls on labeling, design verification, performance testing and cybersecurity. The text states no effective date.
summary.long: 21 CFR § 864.3750 classifies a software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology, an in vitro diagnostic device that uses software algorithms on scanned whole slide images to flag areas with clinical implications, as Class II (special controls). The special controls require that the intended use and labeling state the specimen type, device inputs and outputs, intended users, necessary input/output devices, and limiting statements on adjunct use and on use with complete standard of care evaluation. Labeling must include a detailed device description, a summary of performance testing with stratified sub-analyses, and limiting statements on situations where the device may fail and on interpretation by intended users. Design verification and validation must include a software description with training, tuning and test datasets, emergency recovery functions, a system architecture diagram, and a risk management plan covering cybersecurity. Analytical and clinical studies must document study details, and clinical studies must compare intended users' performance with and without the device using diagnostic accuracy measures. The text states no effective date and contains no penalty or enforcement provisions. Paragraph (b)(3)(iii)(B) is marked [Reserved].
